identity.description: Nonparametric ensemble survival model: bagged trees split by the log-rank statistic, with per-leaf Nelson-Aalen estimators aggregated into per-row survival curves. Captures nonlinearities and interactions no (semi)parametric survival model can, at the cost of coefficient-level interpretability (importances only) and a larger data appetite.

consumes.note: scikit-survival takes the (duration,event) pair as a structured array target (Surv.from_arrays), not as dataframe columns — a wrapper concern, same logical contract

emits.note: predict() returns the ensemble risk score — the aggregated cumulative hazard — the relative-risk ranking that feeds C-index, analogous to Cox's partial hazard but nonlinear in x

predict_survival_function: a per-row STEP function from aggregated leaf Nelson-Aalen estimators — bounded by observed event times, unlike the smooth AFT curves; paramsAsOutput 'none' because the curve is a prediction of the ensemble, not an inspectable parameter table
permutation feature importances (the ImportanceOnly lens) — computed via sklearn permutation_importance against C-index, not a native fitted attribute; caveat: split/diluted under correlated features

n_estimators.note: more trees monotonically stabilize the ensemble curve; diminishing returns, never harmful except in fit time

min_samples_leaf.note: sksurv default 3; the leaf must contain enough EVENTS (not just rows) for a stable per-leaf Nelson-Aalen estimate — the survival-specific reason this matters more than in a regression forest

max_features.note: per-split feature subsampling — the decorrelation knob of bagging

invariances.why: axis-aligned split thresholds depend only on the ORDER of feature values; rescaling changes no split, no tree, no prediction
any strictly monotone per-feature transform preserves value order, hence every candidate split partition — the fit is identical
scikit-survival's tree implementation rejects missing values (raises on NaN) — unlike modern sklearn trees, there is no surrogate/default-direction path

fully nonparametric: no proportional-hazards form, no AFT time-rescaling, no assumed lifetime distribution — log-rank splits plus per-leaf Nelson-Aalen make no functional-form claim; this is where PH/AFT violations route

each leaf needs several EVENTS for a stable Nelson-Aalen estimate and each tree sees a bootstrap subsample — at low event counts trees are shallow and uninformative where a penalized Cox/AFT still estimates
piecewise-constant in feature space (predictions clamp beyond the training range) AND the curve is a step function bounded by observed event times — no tail beyond the data, in either dimension

featureStats.why: THE commit-survival stat: the right-censored fraction is what makes a survival model necessary vs a fixed-window classifier
the effective sample size — RSF specifically needs enough events to populate leaves after bootstrapping; few events routes back to penalized Cox/AFT, not deeper trees
a FAILED Schoenfeld/PH test on the Cox fit is the evidence that buys RSF's nonparametric flexibility — the routing stat INTO this node from the semiparametric branch

modelMetrics.why: the survival-native ranking metric (Harrell's C, natively OOB-estimable via oob_score) — with the ceiling caveat: near-deterministic durations inflate C toward 1, so report with the censoring context
C-index measures ranking only; IBS scores the CALIBRATION of the predicted curves over time — the honest complement for a model whose whole output is per-row curves

edgeCases.behavior: the log-rank split criterion has no signal — no valid split exists
invalid risk sets in the node estimators

edgeCases.condition: few events relative to tree capacity
edgeCases.behavior: leaves with 0-1 events give degenerate Nelson-Aalen estimates; ensemble curves look confident but are noise
edgeCases.note: raise min_samples_leaf / cap max_depth, or route to penalized Cox/AFT

edgeCases.behavior: permutation importances split/dilute across the correlated group — attribution misleads even though prediction is fine
edgeCases.note: interpretation caveat, not a fit failure; report grouped importances

driver.constructor: RandomSurvivalForest(n_estimators=..., min_samples_leaf=..., max_features=..., max_depth=..., n_jobs=-1, random_state=...).fit(X, Surv.from_arrays(event, time))
driver.note: DEP DECISION (tranche-start): scikit-survival is a NEW sidecar dependency, distinct from lifelines which covers the rest of the survival family — flagged for the T4 tranche-start decision (it compiles C extensions and pins a scikit-learn range; the cost is one model's worth unless the ensemble/kernel survival roadmap grows)
driver.wrapperNeeds: adapter: build the sksurv structured-array target Surv.from_arrays(event, duration) from the two target columns (NOT the lifelines df+colnames convention); predict maps to predict (risk score) / predict_survival_function; importances via sklearn permutation_importance; seed threading for reproducible fits
driver.threadSafety: n_jobs-parallel fit (joblib); fitted predict is thread-safe, but never fit the same object concurrently

placementClaims.why: sksurv trees raise on NaN — there is no native missing path, so unimputed rows are a hard failure, not a silent drop
monotone-transform invariant by mechanism — split partitions depend only on value order
scaleSensitive is false by mechanism; scaling changes no split threshold ordering
no native categorical support — categoricals must be numerically encoded before split search
